story.originalTitle: Budkowski replaces Lowdon as Cadillac F1 boss
story.summaryEn: Cadillac Formula 1 Team has appointed Marcin Budkowski as its new team principal, replacing Graeme Lowdon. The 49-year-old previously worked as an aerodynamicist at Prost, Ferrari and McLaren, headed the FIA's F1 technical department, and later joined Renault.
detailZh: 布德科夫斯基接替洛登出任凯迪拉克F1车队领队
马尔钦·布德科夫斯基，曾任阿尔派执行董事，已在这支F1新军接替洛登
凯迪拉克F1车队已聘请新任车队领队，任命马尔钦·布德科夫斯基担任该职位，而非格雷姆·洛登。
49岁的布德科夫斯基在过去25年中在世界锦标赛中担任过多种职务，曾在普罗斯特、法拉利和迈凯伦担任空气动力学专家，之后负责FIA的F1技术部门。
在FIA任职之后，布德科夫斯基加入雷诺车队担任执行董事；他在2021赛季与达维德·布里维奥以双人架构共同分担车队领队职责，随后离开该车队，此后从事咨询和评论工作。
“凯迪拉克F1车队拥有非凡的基础和雄心，”布德科夫斯基说。
“这是车队面临巨大机遇的阶段，其定义将是一个明确的目标：在成本上限内最大化赛车研发，并调动每一个车队职能来参与竞争。
“这意味着建立一个具有赢家心态的精英组织——充满动力，面对挫折不屈不挠，对细节和流程痴迷，并能在比赛日精准执行。
“我的重点将是协调我们的人员、工具和信息流，以便快速做出正确决策，并让我们每次参赛时赛车的性能都有所提升。很荣幸能领导凯迪拉克F1车队的赛道工作，从下周末的赞德沃特开始。”
格雷姆·洛登，凯迪拉克F1车队领队
这位在法国接受教育的波兰人的使命是改善这支垫底车队的命运，因为新车队正在适应F1，并入驻目前正在印第安纳州最终建设的新基础设施。凯迪拉克目前位列车队积分榜末位，尚未获得首个世界锦标赛积分。
“马尔钦的任命标志着凯迪拉克F1车队持续发展的又一重要步骤，”首席执行官丹·托里斯补充道。
“从一开始，我们的目标就不仅仅是参与F1，而是打造一支能够在前列竞争的新一代车队。
“随着我们进入凯迪拉克F1车队的新时代，马尔钦带来了卓越的F1经验、技术专长和战略领导力，这将加强我们的组织，并帮助我们培养长期成功所需的赢家心态、工具和流程。”
布德科夫斯基的任命意味着此前于2024年12月被聘用的车队领队洛登将离开车队。
“我们感谢格雷姆·洛登的领导以及他在从零开始组建凯迪拉克F1车队中所发挥的作用，”托里斯继续说道。
“他的贡献帮助我们在建设阶段奠定了坚实的基础，我们感谢他的付出并祝愿他一切顺利。”
detailEn: Budkowski replaces Lowdon as Cadillac F1 boss
Marcin Budkowski, previously executive director of Alpine, has replaced Lowdon at the debutant F1 outfit
The Cadillac Formula 1 outfit has hired a new team principal, appointing Marcin Budkowski to the position instead of Graeme Lowdon.

Budkowski, 49, has held a myriad of roles in the world championship over the past 25 years, working as an aerodynamicist at Prost, Ferrari and McLaren before heading the FIA’s F1 technical department.

Following his FIA stint, Budkowski joined the Renault squad as an executive director; he shared the team principal duties in a dual set-up alongside Davide Brivio in the 2021 season before leaving the outfit, and has since engaged in consulting and punditry.
“Cadillac Formula 1 Team has an extraordinary foundation and ambition,” Budkowski said.
“This is a phase of huge opportunity for the team, one that will be defined by a clear objective: maximising car development within the cost cap and turning every team function on to compete.
“That means building an elite organisation with a winning mindset - driven, relentless in the face of setbacks, obsessed with detail and process, and able to execute with precision on race day.

“My focus will be on aligning our people, tools and information flow so the right decisions are made quickly, and the performance of the car improves every time we go racing. It is a privilege to be leading Cadillac Formula 1 Team’s on-track efforts, starting in Zandvoort next weekend.”
Graeme Lowdon, Team Principal of Cadillac F1 Team

The French-educated Pole’s mission will be to improve the backmarker’s fortunes as the new team adapts to F1 and settles into new infrastructure currently being finalised in Indiana. Cadillac currently lies last in the constructors’ standings, awaiting its maiden world championship points.
“Marcin's appointment marks another important step in the continued evolution of the Cadillac Formula 1 Team,” CEO Dan Towriss added.
“From the beginning, our goal has not been simply to participate in Formula 1, but to build a next-generation team capable of competing at the very front.

“As we enter this new era for the Cadillac Formula 1 Team, Marcin brings exceptional F1 experience, technical expertise and strategic leadership that will strengthen our organisation and help us develop the winning mindset, tools and processes required for long-term success.”
Budkowski’s appointment means previous team principal Lowdon, who had been hired in December 2024, will leave the team.
“We’re grateful to Graeme Lowdon for his leadership and the role he played in forming the Cadillac Formula 1 Team from the ground up,” Towriss continued.
“His contributions helped establish a strong foundation in our build-up phase, and we thank him for his commitment and wish him well.”

relatedItems.originalTitle: Colton Herta “maybe underestimated the difference” from IndyCar – F2 boss
detailZh: F2总监：赫塔可能低估了F1和IndyCar之间的差距
布鲁诺·米歇尔建议，赫塔在转向F2的过程中遇到了比他预期的更大的困难，但他希望这位美国车手能够反弹。
F2首席执行官布鲁诺·米歇尔表示，赫塔可能低估了F1的二级系列和IndyCar之间的差距，这位26岁的车手的勇敢职业转变至今尚未成功。
赫塔在美国顶级单座赛车系列中一直是领跑者，但决定在2026年回到欧洲——在2015年和2016年参加了跨大西洋的青训车队比赛——以追求他的F1梦想。
在凯迪拉克的F1新车队中获得了测试和开发角色后，赫塔被分配了掌握F2的任务，以便为可能的世界锦标赛晋升做准备。
然而，他在F1的二级系列赛中的首个赛季结果远低于预期。这位加利福尼亚人目前在车手积分榜上排名第19，而且他在整个赛季中的表现水平实际上有所下降——这让他感到困惑——几起事故加剧了他的问题。
“这比我想的要困难得多，因为科尔顿是一个非常强的车手，这一点毫无疑问，”米歇尔评论道。
“他和我们可能低估了我们与IndyCar车队相比的工作环境差异，但我不认为这必须成为一个例子，我真心希望他能够以高水平结束本赛季。我们仍然在为此希望。”
法国人指出，F2复杂的周末赛制，仅有45分钟的自由练习和30分钟的排位赛，可能是赫塔表现不佳的原因之一。
他也有一些不错的比赛，但在排位赛中遇到了更多困难，也许这也是我们遇到的限制之一，因为在30分钟内你需要找到正确的时机[进行你的跑圈]，你只有两次在轮胎上的飞驰圈数，而你在这段有限的时间内几乎没有赛道时间，”米歇尔说。
这也是我们为F1培养车手的方式，因为你知道在F1中你也有有限的赛道时间。
所以，他可能为此而挣扎，并且比他预期的承受了更多的痛苦。现在我真的希望，真诚地希望，他能够以高姿态结束本赛季——他应得的。
赫塔本人对自己的赛季剩余比赛感到不确定，因为卡塔尔和阿布扎比的比赛因伊朗战争而受到威胁，然而米歇尔重申这些赛事“不会取消”。
至于赫塔的未来，Hitech车手明确表示他对第二个F2赛季“没有兴趣”，但他不会排除这种情况，如果凯迪拉克希望他为车队效力。
detailEn: Colton Herta “maybe underestimated the difference” from IndyCar – F2 boss
Bruno Michel suggests Colton Herta struggled “more than what he expected” on his switch to F2 but hopes the American can bounce back
Formula 2 CEO Bruno Michel says Colton Herta “maybe underestimated the difference” between Formula 1’s feeder series and IndyCar, with the 26-year-old’s bold career move so far unsuccessful.

Herta was a frontrunner in America’s premier single-seater series for seven years but decided to move back to Europe in 2026 – having competed in junior formulae across the pond in 2015 and 2016 – in order to chase his F1 dream.
Having landed a test and development role with Cadillac’s nascent F1 team, Herta was tasked with mastering F2 in order to prepare for a potential graduation to the world championship.

However, his maiden season in F1’s feeder series has ended up well below expectations. The Californian lies 19th in the drivers’ standings, and his performance level has actually worsened throughout the year – which he has been at a loss to explain – with several crashes compounding his issues.
“It's been more difficult than what I thought it was going to be, because Colton is a very strong driver, there's no doubt about that,” Michel commented.

“He and we maybe underestimated the difference of working environment that we had compared to IndyCar teams, but I don't think it has to be settled as an example, and I really hope that he's going to finish the season in a high. We're still hoping for that.”
The Frenchman pointed to F2’s tricky weekend format, with just a 45-minute free practice session and a 30-minute qualifying round ahead of the two races, as a potential cause for Herta’s struggle.

“He had some good races as well, he had more difficulties in quali, and maybe also that's one of the limits that we were having, because in 30 minutes you come up with the right timing [for your runs], you have two flying laps on sets of tyres on which you have very limited track time,” Michel said.
“That's also the way we prepare drivers for Formula 1, because you know in Formula 1 that you have limited track time as well.
“So, probably he struggled for that and he suffered from that a bit more than what he expected. Now I really hope, sincerely, that he's going to finish the season on a high – he deserves it.”

Herta himself was unsure he was going to get any more races to finish the season given the Qatar and Abu Dhabi rounds are known to be at threat due to the Iran war, however Michel reaffirmed these events “will not be cancelled”.
As for Herta’s future, the Hitech driver made it clear that he had “no interest” in a sophomore F2 season, but he won’t rule it out in case that’s what Cadillac wants for him.
